newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan exchange delists investment firm.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan exchange delists investment firm.

text.p: Morocco has reduced the number of listed companies on the Casablanca bourse to 46 after it delisted Omnium Marocain d'Investissement firm (OMI), brokers said on Wednesday.
"OMI firm was delisted following a recent decision taken by the bourse watchdog Conseil Deontologique des Valeurs Mobilieres (CDVM)," a stockbroker at Casablanca Finance Intermediation said.
The decision was effective from October 17, 1996, he added.
A bourse spokeswoman confirmed the information but declined to comment.

To comply with CDVM rules, listed firms are obliged to publish their half-year and annual results if they want to remain on the bourse. "OMI firm -- which was not a liquid stock -- did not apparently comply with the bourse rules," a market analyst said.

Established in the financial centre of Casablanca since 1929, the bourse had an average monthly trading volume of 500 million dirhams ($58.1 million) and 1.2 million shares in the first 10 months of 1996, officials said.
